videos.displayTitle: Trying Box Hill’s most adventurous Asian…
videos.description:
In today’s video, we explore Box Hill, one of Melbourne’s most iconic hubs for Asian food. From the busy food courts inside Box Hill Central to the hidden gems along the streets, this area is packed with flavours you won’t find anywhere else.

We kick things off at Magic Cuisine, a spot known for its adventurous organ dishes like tripe salad and pigs’ ear mix. Then it’s over to Wok In Walk Out, an unsuspecting takeaway joint serving homely Chinese classics like pork egg cake and spicy Sichuan tofu.

Next, we try a fried pork bao bursting with juicy flavour, followed by something daring — ox tongue and pork intestines from Rainbow Chicken. These might sound intimidating, but the rich flavours will surprise you.

To finish, we explore Uyghur cuisine at Silk Road, where we taste a creamy haggis soup and some of the best lamb skewers in Melbourne — perfectly spiced, smoky, and tender.

If you’re looking to explore authentic Asian eats and discover something different in Melbourne, Box Hill is the place to go.

Box Hill is a bustling suburb in Melbourne, Victoria, about 14 km east of the CBD. It’s a vibrant, multicultural hub known for its commercial vibrancy, diverse dining scene, and excellent transport links. Here’s a quick rundown:
Location & Vibe: Situated in the City of Whitehorse, Box Hill is a melting pot of cultures, particularly with a strong Asian influence, reflected in its restaurants, markets, and community events.
Key Features:
Box Hill Central: A major shopping complex with over 200 stores, including major retailers, supermarkets, and specialty shops. It’s a focal point for both locals and visitors.
Dining: Famous for its Asian cuisine, especially Chinese, Korean, and Vietnamese restaurants. Popular spots include Tien Dat for phở and Shanghai Street for dumplings.
Transport: A major transport hub with Box Hill railway station (on the Belgrave and Lilydale lines) and a bus interchange. It’s well-connected to the CBD and surrounding suburbs.
Education: Home to Box Hill Institute and close to several schools, making it popular with students.
Health: Box Hill Hospital is a significant medical facility in the area.
Parks & Recreation: Nearby parks like Box Hill Gardens and Surrey Park offer green spaces for relaxation and sports.
Cultural Significance: The suburb hosts events like the Chinese New Year Festival, and its multicultural fabric makes it a lively place year-round.
Recent Developments: Box Hill has seen ongoing growth with high-rise apartments and commercial developments, boosting its urban feel while maintaining community charm.

We’re making great progress on construction of SRL East in Box Hill.

Crews worked around the clock last month to move and upgrade the 109 tram stop on Whitehorse Road in Box Hill, so tram services can continue while SRL East is built.

Our team will soon build a temporary bridging structure to keep traffic flowing on Whitehorse Road during construction.

Box Hill is a suburb of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, 14 kilometres (8.7 mi) east of the city's Central Business District (CBD),[2] located within the City of Whitehorse local government area. Box Hill recorded a population of 14,353 at the 2021 census.

Founded as a township in the 1850s, Box Hill grew over the following century into a small city with its own CBD, its own municipality in the former City of Box Hill, and its own suburbs, including Box Hill North and Box Hill South. In the 1950s, Box Hill was absorbed into Melbourne as part of the eastward expansion of the metropolis. Today, Box Hill is notable for its large Chinese community, being one of the largest in Melbourne, and is home to the city's tallest high-rise buildings outside the CBD.

A major transportation hub for Melbourne's eastern suburbs, Box Hill is home of one of the city's busiest train stations, located beneath Box Hill Central. It is also served by the route 109 tram and numerous bus routes.

Credit: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box_Hill,_Victoria

Box Hill is a suburb of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, 14 kilometres (8.7 mi) east of the city's Central Business District (CBD),[2] located within the City of Whitehorse local government area. Box Hill recorded a population of 14,353 at the 2021 census.

Founded as a township in the 1850s, Box Hill grew over the following century into a small city with its own CBD, its own municipality in the former City of Box Hill, and its own suburbs, including Box Hill North and Box Hill South. In the 1950s, Box Hill was absorbed into Melbourne as part of the eastward expansion of the metropolis. Today, Box Hill is notable for its large Chinese community, being one of the largest in Melbourne, and is home to the city's tallest high-rise buildings outside the CBD.

channelMasterConfig.tickerText: BOX HILL IS ONE OF MELBOURNE’S MOST DISTINCTIVE AND FAST-EVOLVING SUBURBAN CENTRES, LOCATED AROUND 14 KILOMETRES EAST OF THE CBD. ONCE A QUIET VILLAGE SURROUNDED BY ORCHARDS AND FARMLAND, TODAY IT’S A BUZZING MIX OF OLD MELBOURNE, MODERN HIGH-RISE LIVING AND ONE OF THE CITY’S GREAT ASIAN FOOD PRECINCTS. WHITEHORSE ROAD AND BOX HILL CENTRAL FORM THE HEART OF THE SUBURB, PACKED WITH RESTAURANTS, NOODLE SHOPS, BAKERIES, GROCERIES AND SMALL BUSINESSES. BOX HILL IS ALSO A MAJOR TRANSPORT HUB, WITH TRAINS, TRAMS AND BUSES CONNECTING IT ACROSS MELBOURNE. BEYOND THE BUSY CENTRE YOU’LL FIND LEAFY RESIDENTIAL STREETS, PARKS, SPORTING CLUBS, BOX HILL GARDENS AND PLENTY OF REMINDERS OF THE AREA’S HISTORY. IT’S BUSY, MULTICULTURAL, SOMETIMES CHAOTIC AND CONSTANTLY CHANGING — A SUBURB THAT HAS GROWN INTO A DESTINATION IN ITS OWN RIGHT.
